Let \(s_i=A_iA_{i+1}\) with \(A_{n+1}=A_1\), and let \(\theta=\frac{2\pi}{n}\). Since the polygon is equiangular, the side vectors have directions \(0,\theta,2\theta,\dots,(n-1)\theta\). Closure gives
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n s_i(\cos(i-1)\theta,\sin(i-1)\theta)=0.
\]
Taking the \(y\)-component:
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n s_i\sin((i-1)\theta)=0.
\]
Pair \(i\) with \(n+2-i\). For each \(i\) with \(\sin((i-1)\theta)>0\),
\[
\sin((n+1-i)\theta)=-\sin((i-1)\theta),
\]
so the imaginary part becomes
\[
\sum (s_i-s_{n+2-i})\sin((i-1)\theta)=0.
\]
By monotonicity \(s_i\le s_{n+2-i}\), and the sine factors are positive, so every term is \(\le 0\). Hence each term is \(0\). In particular, \(s_2=s_n\). Then
\[
s_2\le s_3\le\cdots\le s_n=s_2
\]
forces \(s_2=s_3=\cdots=s_n\). Closure then forces \(s_1=s_2\). Thus all sides are equal.

Therefore \(A_1A_n=A_nA_1=A_1A_2\), so
\[
\frac{A_1A_n}{A_1A_2}=1.
\]

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
